# Adding us-west-2 to Crossplane via Provider Config

Crossplane supports multiple provider configs per provider. We add a second `ProviderConfig` (and its provider install/deployment) for us-west-2, then reference it from the prod S3 bucket's replication config — **no existing claims change**.

## 1. Second provider install (separate deployment per region)

```yaml
# crossplane/providers/provider-aws-usw2.yaml
apiVersion: pkg.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Provider
metadata:
  name: provider-aws-us-west-2
spec:
  package: xpkg.upbound.io/upbound/provider-aws-s3:v1.2.1
  controllerConfigRef:
    name: provider-aws-usw2-config
---
apiVersion: pkg.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: ControllerConfig
metadata:
  name: provider-aws-usw2-config
spec:
  podAnnotations:
   .region: us-west-2
```

## 2. Second ProviderConfig

```yaml
# crossplane/configs/provider-config-usw2.yaml
apiVersion: aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-west-2
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-creds            # same secret works; region is per-config
      key: creds
  region: us-west-2
```

Existing resources keep `providerConfigRef.name: default` — untouched.

## 3. Prod composition patch: replication destination bucket

```yaml
# crossplane/compositions/replica-bucket-patch.yaml
# In the prod composition (or prod composition patch), add a replica bucket
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: app-assets-replica-usw2
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: aws-us-west-2          # <-- routes to us-west-2
  forProvider:
    region: us-west-2
---
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: s3-replication-role
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
  forProvider:
    assumeRolePolicy: |
      {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow",
       "Principal":{"Service":"s3.amazonaws.com"},
       "Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}
---
apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: RolePolicy
metadata:
  name: s3-replication-policy
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
  forProvider:
    roleRef: s3-replication-role
    policy: |
      {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":[
        "s3:GetReplicationConfiguration","s3:ListBucket",
        "s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication","s3:GetObjectVersionAcl",
        "s3:GetObjectVersionTagging","s3:ReplicateObject",
        "s3:ReplicateDelete","s3:ReplicateTags"],
       "Resource":"*"}]}
```

## 4. Attach replication rule to prod primary bucket

```yaml
# Patch to prod bucket resource in the composition:
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketVersioning
metadata:
  name: app-assets-prod
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
  forProvider:
    bucketRef:
      name: app-assets-prod
    versioningConfiguration:
      status: Enabled
---
apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: BucketReplicationConfiguration
metadata:
  name: app-assets-prod-repl
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default
  forProvider:
    bucketRef:
      name: app-assets-prod
    region: us-east-1           # primary region
    roleRef: s3-replication-role
    rule:
      - destination:
          - bucketRef:
              name: app-assets-replica-usw2
            storageClass: STANDARD
        status: Enabled
        filter: {}              # whole bucket
```

## Verification

```bash
kubectl get providerconfig aws-us-west-2 -o yaml
kubectl get providerrevision -l pkg.crossplane.io/provider=provider-aws-us-west-2
# Confirm dev untouched:
kubectl get bucket -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PROVIDER:.spec.providerConfigRef.name
# Expect: only prod + replica reference aws-us-west-2
```

**Key points:** claims and XRDs are untouched — region selection is a provider-config-level concern; environment isolation holds because dev resources still bind to `default`. The replication IAM policy `*` on Resource is scoped to replication actions only (acceptable; prod app roles remain least-privilege).
